issue.title: Inheritance messes up constructor injection

labels.name: area: core
labels.description: Issues related to the framework runtime

issue.body:
When using component inheritance (which e.g. Meteor 2 Angular is based on right now), dependency injection can be tricky. First off, it seems like constructor injection is a bad choice for that use case, as it's easy for derived components to forget to pass DI parameters to the super class. Also, all dependencies propagate down, which makes it hard to introduce new dependencies in base classes. 

So, first question: Is this right? Is property injection somehow available? Maybe you'd recommend a manual approach, i.e. something like

```
Injector.resolveAndCreate([MyType]).get(MyType)
```

Second, even if running with constructor injection, it's sort of fine, as typescript passes along the requirements down to child components (you'll get typescript errors if you don't pass the args) if you declare a constructor. But...that only works as long as you declare a constructor. If not, it's silent and you're screwed. I don't see any easy fixes as I don't know a way to identify Typescript autogenerated constructors, look up the super class, and generate injection parameters for that.

Thoughts on best practices pattern? The current seems error prone.

issue.title: Support @Input(), @Output(), @HostBinding() defined in superclasses and mixins
issue.body:
Lifecycle interfaces implementations in superclasses seem to be already supported (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/4222)

It would be great for `@Input()`, `@Output()`, `@HostBinding()` to also be supported for reusable implementations (like behaviors in Polymer).

issue.title: OnInit is not respecting inheritance
issue.body:
Suppose you have this class hierarchy
A
|
B
and A implements OnInit but B does not explicitly declare that it implements OnInit, only that it extends A.  Then angular will (incorrectly) not call ngOnInit when it creates an instance of B.

issue.title: Input decorators not working in extended class
issue.body:
I have an abstract class with an @Input() decorator on a property, and when I extend that class I add a second @Input() decorator on a different property. The property on the original abstract class is not on the instance when it compiles. However when I remove the second property's decorator the first works again.

I would expect that both bindings would work however I'm not sure whether the issue is as I have outlined or that you can in some cases bind an @Input() on an abstract class.

P.S. I am using an abstract class as multiple classes have the same logic (as they are all input types), however I am aware that on its own @Input() doesn't make sense on an abstract class.

issue.title: When decorating class, Dependency infection is not respected...
Overridden component classes and @Input() properties
@Input and @Output annotations are not carried from subclasses
issue.body:
It would be nice if `@Input` and `@Output` annotations are carried from subclassed components. Currently this doesn't work with Transformers because it only looks at the local file.

I'm guessing we may not need to parse the Subclass directly, but might be able to look up the information that is saved from it's parent.
